title: Termapy Device Profile
description: Declarative description of a serial device for the termapy MCP bridge. Profiles describe the four supported response patterns plus transport noise handling. Behavior beyond pattern matching belongs in scripts, not profiles.

profile_version.description: Schema version. 2 = v2 (top-level transport/device/error_detection blocks). Absent = treat as v1 (commands-only, backward compatible).

profile_revision.description: Per-profile semver revision (e.g. "1.4.0"). Used in precedence comparisons against device-fetched manifests. Absent = treat as 0.0.0.

profile_date.description: ISO 8601 date the profile was authored/edited. Tiebreaker when revisions are equal. Absent = treat as epoch.

version.description: Legacy v1 commands-dict version field. Ignored by v2 readers; kept for backward compat round-trip.

startup_banner.description: Regex matching the device's banner after connect or reset. Bridge logs match/non-match; never blocks.

prompt.description: Trailing prompt string (e.g. ">", "# "). Used as default response terminator when set. Empty = no prompt.

transport.description: Wire-level rules: serial parameters, framing, noise handling. Applied to the live session when the profile loads in MCP mode.

protocol.description: Wire format. ndjson = JSON object per line. text = templated text in/out.

line_ending_send.description: Line ending appended to outbound text commands. Common values: "\n", "\r\n", "\r".

line_ending_recv.description: Line ending used to split inbound text. Default: "\n".

echo.description: True if device echoes inbound bytes; bridge strips the echoed line from response.

inter_command_delay_ms.description: Minimum gap between consecutive serial sends, regardless of source. Bridge enforces.

default_response_timeout_ms.description: Fallback timeout for commands without explicit response.timeout_ms.

field_routing.description: NDJSON-only: which JSON fields the bridge uses to auto-route inbound messages. Defaults: response_id=id, error_field=error, event_field=event. Override only if device uses different conventions.

error_detection.description: Global error pattern. Applied to every response after per-command parsing. Async-flagged matches without an in-flight command route to device_state.async_errors.

pattern.description: Regex matching the error indicator in device output. Named groups recommended (e.g. (?P<code>\d+)).

async.description: True if errors can arrive unsolicited between commands.

codes.description: Map of error code (string) to human-readable meaning. Used for context in error messages.

types.description: Type coercion for named regex groups. Same vocabulary as response.types.

commands.description: Command catalog. Keys are command names as the device expects them.

command.description: A single device command. Only `help` is required; everything else is optional. v1 manifests with just help/args/long_help/flags continue to work.

args.description: Argument spec for help display (legacy v1 shape).

flags.description: Map of flag name to description (v1 shape).

typed_args.description: v2: structured argument schemas for codegen and validation.

send_template.description: v2: how to format the outbound bytes. Python-format style with named placeholders, e.g. "AT+VOLT={mv}". Empty = use the command name verbatim. For NDJSON protocol, the bridge serializes args as a JSON object instead.

safety.description: v2: safety tier. readonly = pure observation; safe = default, no enduring effect; mutable = changes device state but reversible (LED toggle, set baud); destructive = irreversible / data-loss (factory reset, flash erase, file delete). Only destructive triggers the MCP confirmation gate; other tiers are documentation-only metadata.

rate_limit_hz.description: v2: bridge-enforced rate limit. 0 = no limit.

timeout_ms.description: v2: per-command timeout override (separate from response.timeout_ms which is the wait-for-response window). 0 = use config default.

typed_arg.description: A single argument descriptor. Matches the shape of a function parameter for codegen.

response.description: How to interpret the device's response. The four patterns + none.

format.description: Response shape. none=fire-and-forget. literal=must equal pattern. lines=collect until terminator. regex=match pattern (named groups become typed dict). json=parse as JSON.

pattern.description: Regex (for format=regex/lines line-filter) or literal string (for format=literal).

terminator.description: For format=lines: regex matching the line that ends collection (e.g. "^OK$"). Overrides transport.prompt for this command.

line_pattern.description: For format=lines: optional regex with named groups applied to each line, producing a list of dicts.

line_types.description: Type coercion for line_pattern named groups.

types.description: For format=regex: type coercion for named groups in pattern.
